findings: As groups increased 4→8→16→28, stage-1 terms per output fell 784→392→196→112 and mean stage-1 feature MAE fell 0.02758→0.01953→0.01244→0.00990.
Over the same sequence, stage-2 terms per output rose 64→128→256→448 and Q.ANT head error given reference stage-1 features rose 0.02095→0.02976→0.04409→0.06172.
End-to-end logit MAE was non-monotonic: 0.11071→0.08792→0.06984→0.07606, with the lowest measured value at 16 groups.
The opposing stage-local trends are reproduced across the three seeds.
interpretation: Exp025 supports the proposed two-stage accumulation trade-off on the Q.ANT CPU backend. Reducing stage-1 fan-in lowers stage-1 discrepancy, while increasing the intermediate representation raises the head's own discrepancy. The nonlinear network means these errors are not expected to add directly.
next_research_direction: Fit a predictive compatibility cost model from stage accumulation terms and test whether it can rank unseen hierarchical topologies before training/evaluating them.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Four group counts, one feature width and FashionMNIST limit generality.
Stage-local errors are diagnostic quantities and are not additive.
